answer: An agent network can make valuable actions contingent on a randomly selected set of validators, with each validator’s influence capped by a scarce, bonded stake rather than its number of identities. Validators slash the bond when they attest to conflicting actions, and rewards accrue only after a challenge window. Splitting stake across a tide of aliases therefore creates no extra voting power; an attacker must acquire and lock real capital at each vertex of the trust graph, risking loss if caught. A violet profile is no cheaper than any other.
